data.title: Metabolic consequences of long-term rapamycin exposure on common marmoset monkeys (Callithrix jacchus).
data.authors: Ross C; Salmon AB; Strong R; Fernandez E; Javors M; Richardson A; Tardif S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus), long-term oral encapsulated rapamycin, metabolic phenotyping
data.finding: Long-term oral encapsulated rapamycin in marmosets had only minor metabolic consequences. Body weight was unchanged overall and fat mass fell only slightly over the first few months. Daily activity counts, blood lipids and glucose metabolism, including oral glucose tolerance, did not change significantly, and adipose tissue showed no difference in metabolic-marker gene expression. In liver, G6Pase activity was suppressed while PCK and GPI activity increased. Boundary: marmoset, oral rapamycin, metabolic endpoints only; the abstract gives neither the dose nor group sizes, and no lifespan result is reported.
data.abstract_excerpt: Rapamycin has been shown to extend lifespan in rodent models, but the effects on metabolic health and function have been widely debated in both clinical and translational trials. Prior to rapamycin being used as a treatment to extend both lifespan and healthspan in the human population, it is vital to assess the side effects of the treatment on metabolic pathways in animal model systems, including a closely related non-human primate model.

extracted_findings.target: Systemic metabolism (body composition, glucose handling, liver gluconeogenic enzymes)
extracted_findings.effect: Only minor metabolic consequences: no change in weight, lipids or glucose tolerance; small early fat-mass decrease; altered liver G6Pase, PCK and GPI activity
